Given that the ray above passes through the point with Cartesian coordinates $(-6,-2\sqrt{3})$, find the polar equation of the ray.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the reference angle associated with the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{-2\sqrt{3}}{-6}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the ray lies in the third quadrant. So, we find the angle in the third quadrant that has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar equation of the ray is 

$$
\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6}.
$$
